To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the HBV subgenotyping in Southeast Brazil revealed a high prevalence of genotype D, with subgenotype D1, D3, and D4; (2) the phylogenetic trees showed that the sequences obtained interweaves with sequences from other regions of the world, corresponding to the countries from where many immigrants have come to this region; (3) eight families whose relatives have been infected with the same genotype were identified, with sequences with a high similarity between them.
the HBV sequences from RibeirãoPreto interweaved with HBV sequences from other continents.
the most prevalent subgenotype in Ribeirao Preto, Brazil is D3 and the sequences found were similar to those from Italy.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the genetic variability of the HBV in a Brazilian region, with the history of intense immigration of Italian people, and the distribution of the subgenotypes found was in agreement with the hypothesis that the virus was brought during the colonization period.
the distribution of HBV genotypes/subgenotypes in Southeast Brazil and the possible influence of Italian immigration in this region.
the distribution of HBV subtypes in Ribeirâo Preto, a region with a history of intense Italian and European immigration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HBV subgenotyping of this region reflects the history of immigration to Brazil.
HBV genotypes A, D, F, and subgenotypes A2, D3 and D4, are present in Southeastern Brazil.
the HBV sequences found in this region are the result of a complex history of migration of people from all over the world.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genetic diversity of HBV found in Ribeirao Preto, Brazil, reflects the history of the region.
the HBV subgenotyping in Ribeirao Preto, Brazil, is a mosaic of sequences from Europe, Africa and Asia.

the HBV genotypic distribution in Ribeirao Preto, a region with history intense of Italian immigration, is similar to that found in Italy, suggesting a possible influence of the Italian migration in the HBV genotyping found in this region of Southeastern Brazil.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic diversity of HBV is a consequence of the history of the human population.
HBV genotype D3 was the main genotype found in our population.

the distribution of the different HBV subgenotypies in Brazil, and in particular, in Ribeirao Preto, is not homogeneous, with some subgenotypes being predominant in some regions and others being found in different areas, suggesting the existence of a history of HBV introduction and circulation.
